qAndA.answer: Because they have a giant structure with lots of strong ionic bonds. A lot of energy is required to break these bonds.
qAndA.question: Why do ionic compounds have high melting and boiling points?

qAndA.answer: No, not all ionic compounds are soluble in water, but many are. Salt (sodium chloride) is a good example of a soluble ionic compound.
qAndA.question: Can all ionic compounds dissolve in water?

qAndA.answer: Ionic compounds can conduct electricity when they are dissolved in water or when they are molten. This is because the charged ions are free to move.
qAndA.question: When can ionic compounds conduct electricity?
